answer: Answer: Original-study effect sizes tend to be larger than replication effect sizes in ALL three domains — Cognitive psychology, Social psychology, and (Experimental) Economics — and the pattern is statistically significant in each. The absolute Fisher-z gap is similar for Cognitive (mean |fisr|−|fiso| = −0.23, 82% of pairs smaller, Wilcoxon p ≈ 1e-5; meta-analytic d = −0.23 [−0.33, −0.14]) and Social (−0.20, 88% of pairs smaller, p ≈ 1e-5; meta-analytic d = −0.22 [−0.29, −0.15]), and somewhat smaller but still significant in Economics (−0.24 mean, 83% of pairs, Wilcoxon p = 0.0008; meta-analytic d = −0.13 [−0.25, −0.01], p = 0.03; n = 18, interpret cautiously). On the RELATIVE scale, however, Social psychology shows by far the strongest attenuation (median relative_es = 0.13, i.e., replications recover ~13% of the original effect) versus Cognitive (0.65) and Economics (0.70) — because Social original effects are smallest in absolute terms (mean |fiso| = 0.37) so a similar absolute drop is a larger proportional loss. Overall: 85% of the 86 pairs have |fisr| < |fiso|; pooled meta-analytic difference −0.21 [−0.26, −0.16]. Sensitivity checks (Eitam/Hassin row removed; signed vs absolute differences; project-level cut) leave all conclusions unchanged.

payload.hypothesis: Original-study effect estimates are systematically larger than replication estimates in every domain in the data — Cognitive psychology, Social psychology, and (Experimental) Economics — with 85% of the 86 original–replication pairs showing a smaller absolute Fisher-z effect in the replication (all three within-domain Wilcoxon signed-rank p ≤ 0.001). The absolute attenuation gap is similar for Cognitive (mean −0.23; meta-analytic −0.23 [−0.33, −0.14]) and Social psychology (−0.20; meta-analytic −0.22 [−0.29, −0.15]) and somewhat smaller in Economics (−0.24; meta-analytic −0.13 [−0.25, −0.01], p = 0.03, n = 18). On the relative scale, however, Social psychology shows the strongest attenuation (median relative effect size 0.13, i.e., replications recover only ~13% of the original effect) compared with Cognitive (0.65) and Economics (0.70), because Social original effects are smallest in absolute terms. Thus, no domain is spared — originals are larger everywhere — but Social psychology exhibits the largest proportional loss and Economics the mildest.
payload.workflow: Inspected the 86-row joined meta-regression dataset (all schema columns present; zero missingness in ro/rr/fiso/fisr/discipline/project.x; verified fiso=atanh(ro) and fisr=atanh(rr); flagged 18 sign-flipped replications and one anomalous relative_es entry). Main analysis (artifacts/analysis_main.py): per row computed |fisr|−|fiso| (primary, magnitude framing for sign flips) and signed fisr−fiso (secondary); per discipline and per project reported means/medians, mean/median relative_es, and % of pairs with |fisr|<|fiso|; paired Wilcoxon signed-rank and paired t-tests per domain; DerSimonian–Laird random-effects meta-analysis of the signed z-difference with var = se_fisr²+se_fiso² per domain; sensitivity analyses excluding the Eitam/Hassin row and comparing signed vs absolute differences. Conclusions robust across all checks.
